memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: When Arphaxad had lived 35 years, he became the father of Shelah... When Shelah had lived 30 years, he became the father of Eber... When Eber had lived 34 years, he became the father of Peleg... - Gen 11:12-17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Arphaxad, Shelah, Eber, Peleg - names that mean little to us, lives reduced to a line each. They were born, they had children, they lived, they died. No great deeds are recorded, no famous moments. And yet each one was a vital link in the chain that would lead to Abraham, and eventually to Jesus Christ. Without these ordinary lives, there would be no Saviour.

That is worth sitting with. God's greatest work in history ran straight through the lives of people whose stories we do not know. They were not famous. They did not build towers or found empires. They simply lived, raised families, and passed on life to the next generation - and God used them.

If you have ever felt that your life is too ordinary to matter, look at this list. God's plan of salvation depended on people exactly like you: unremarkable to the world, faithful in their own small span, entirely known to God.

Notice too the shortening lifespans as the list goes on - the effects of the fall pressing down through the generations. Yet God's purposes were undiminished. Human frailty could not slow His plan. Every one of these names mattered, because God had chosen to work through them. Your ordinary faithfulness matters too. "Whatever you do, work at it with all your heart, as working for the Lord" (Col 3:23). God builds His purposes with lives like yours.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you believe your ordinary life matters in God's plan?
- What are you passing on to the generation after you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, thank You that You work Your purposes through ordinary, unremarkable lives. Help me be faithful in my span of years, and to pass on something of You to those who follow.
Amen.
